text.p: These are the highlights of
the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- SISCOMEX HURTS THE INDUSTRY
The Siscomex computerized system for imports was a headache for Brazilian companies in its first week of operations.
-- BIS INVITES BRAZIL TO JOIN ITS "BOARD"

Brazil is about to join the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), the bank of the central banks based in Basle, Switzerland. The BIS includes 33 central banks of the most developed economies in the world.
-- GASOLINE, GOV'T BREAKS OLIGOPOLY
Gas stations will be allowed to purchase fuel from any distributor, said the Energy and Mines Minister Raimundo Brito. - - -
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- FHC SEEKS 108 VOTES FOR RE-ELECTION

The Fernando Henrique Cardoso government has at least 200 votes in favor of the re-election amendment in the Chamber of Deputies, according to a poll by Folha. The newspaper interviewed 481 of 513 deputies.
The government needs 308 votes to have the amendment which would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for a second term approved.
-- TAX RECEIPTS HIT A RECORD IN 1996
Brazil's tax receipts hit a record 97.5 billion reais in 1996, according to the Internal Revenue Service. Companies paid 13.284 billion reais in tax income, a rise of 24.14 percent over 1995.
O GLOBO
-- GOV'T WILL INVESTIGATE EXCESSIVE INCREASES IN BANKING FEES
The Justice Ministry's consumer defense department will investigate into allegations that banks are overcharging for their banking services.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom 5511-2485412))
